passage: In the colony park, Yusuf ran to the swing and shouted, "My turn!" Hafsa held the chains tighter and swung higher. Yusuf shouted louder and got only a shrug, so he kicked the pole and went home. The next day he stood by the swing for a while, then tried something different. "Can I go after you?" "Okay," said Hafsa. "Ten more swings." Yusuf sat on the bench and counted along with her. When his turn came, he swung hard and grinned. On Friday he asked the same way again.

qa.q: What did Yusuf ask Hafsa the next day?
qa.a: Yusuf asked, "Can I go after you?"

qa.q: What was Yusuf feeling when he kicked the pole and went home?
qa.a: Yusuf felt frustrated and cross, because shouting had got him nowhere.

qa.q: What other approach could Yusuf add, and why?
qa.a: He could offer a trade, like "I push you, then you push me." A trade gives Hafsa something too, so it is easier for Hafsa to say yes.

qa.q: How do the two ways of asking look to Hafsa?
qa.a: Shouting sounds like a demand, so holding on tighter is natural. Asking politely leaves the choice with Hafsa, so Hafsa agrees and sets the count.

grounding: A child whose shouting failed asks politely the next day and keeps polite asking as the new plan.
